digest.top_line: RTOG 0848: adjuvant CXRT misses OS (HR 0.96), but N0 pts show 5y OS 48.1% vs 28.6% (interaction P=.0063).
digest.tldr: Upper GI carried the day alone. RTOG 0848 answers the adjuvant pancreas RT question negatively overall, then reopens it in node-negative disease, where 50.4 Gy/28 fx with modern QA (81% IMRT, 92% per-protocol) tracked with near-doubled 5y OS in 91 pts. Hypothesis-generating, not practice-changing, and the backbone was gemcitabine-era.

sites.intro: First modern-QA randomised read on adjuvant chemoradiation after resected pancreatic cancer: negative overall, with an N0 signal that ESPAC-1's split-course 2D design could never have isolated.

studies.name: NRG Oncology/RTOG 0848
studies.tldr: OS HR 0.96 (90% CI 0.79-1.18), primary endpoint missed; node-negative interaction p=.0063 favors adjuvant CXRT.
details: 📊 1° EP OS not met: HR 0.96 (90% CI 0.79-1.18), one-sided P=.38, two-sided P=.77
📊 Median OS 2.6y (2.1-3.1) chemo vs 2.3y (2.0-2.6) chemo+CXRT; 5y 23.1% vs 27.9%
📊 DFS trend favoring CXRT: HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.65-1.03), P=.089
📊 Treatment × nodal status interaction: OS P=.0063, DFS P=.014, benefit confined to N0

details.text: 📊 Node-negative subgroup (n=91), CXRT vs chemo alone

details: 🔍 Two-step phase III: step 2 randomized 354 pts (174 chemo, 180 chemo+CXRT) after 5 cycles without progression
🔍 RT was 50.4 Gy/28 fx to tumor bed, pancreatojejunostomy and regional nodes; 81% IMRT, 19% 3D conformal
🔍 Real-time central RT review pre-treatment; overall per-protocol/acceptable in 142/155 treated (92%)
🔍 Sensitizer 83% capecitabine, 15% infusional 5-FU; 88% of the 153 treated got ≥50 Gy
⚠️ 25 of 180 assigned to CXRT (14%) never received it, 18 by refusal; as-treated HR 0.98 (90% CI 0.80-1.20)
⚠️ Grade 3 AEs 38% vs 19%, P<.001, driven by GI/diarrhea and lymphopenia; grade 4/5 unchanged (6% v 5%, P=.68)
⚠️ Nodal-status interaction is a subgroup finding, hypothesis-generating; only 91 N0 pts (26%)
⚠️ Backbone is gemcitabine-era: 67% gemcitabine alone, 28% gem+erlotinib, zero FOLFIRINOX
🔗 vs ESPAC-1, where CXRT was detrimental: that trial used split-course lower dose, 2D planning, no QA, accrual 1994-2000
🔗 Failure pattern in this cohort: distant-only first failure 38%, local-only 23%

verdict.rationale: Randomized phase III, prespecified stratification by nodal status, primary OS negative; the N0 benefit is a subgroup interaction needing confirmation on modern systemic backbones.
verdict.audience: Resected pancreatic head adenocarcinoma, R0/R1, post 5 cycles adjuvant chemo

studies.significance: The RT-relevant read is the nodal interaction: in N0 pts (n=91) median OS 3.9y vs 3.0y and 5y OS 48.1% vs 28.6%, with 50.4 Gy/28 fx to bed plus regional nodes under real-time central QA. That is the population where adjuvant CXRT is worth discussing, and the QA'd modern technique is what separates this from ESPAC-1.
studies.monday_clinic: In resected node-negative pancreatic head adenocarcinoma completing adjuvant chemotherapy without progression, this supports discussing adjuvant chemoradiation; it does not apply to node-positive disease, where no treatment effect was seen.

primary_endpoint.name: Overall survival
primary_endpoint.stat_detail: 90% CI 0.79-1.18, one-sided P=.38; primary endpoint not met

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Multicenter randomized **phase IIR/III**, two-step. Step 1 gemcitabine ± erlotinib; step 2 randomized 1:1 to a sixth chemotherapy cycle **± CXRT** after five cycles without progression. Accrual November 2009 to October 2018, analyzed December 2023; median follow-up 2.2 y overall, **7.4 y in survivors**.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Curative-intent resection of **pancreatic head** adenocarcinoma with gross total resection on the operative note and documented microscopic margin status; body/tail excluded per RTOG 9704. N=354 (174 v 180), median age 63, 56% Zubrod 1, **74% node-positive**, 17% margin-positive, 81% pT3, 96% postresection CA19-9 ≤90.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Step 1 backbone was **gemcitabine alone in 67%**, gemcitabine + erlotinib 28%, non-oxaliplatin gemcitabine combinations 5%, and **no FOLFIRINOX/mFOLFIRINOX**. Sensitization was capecitabine in 83% and infusional 5-FU in 15%; 5% and 17% respectively stopped the sensitizer for toxicity.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **50.4 Gy in 28 fractions** starting within 21 days of cycle 6, targeting tumor bed, pancreatojejunostomy and **regional nodes**. Median delivered dose 50.4 Gy (range 7.2-50.4), 28 fractions, 38 days elapsed; 81% IMRT, 19% 3D conformal, 79% with no interruption. Centers were IROC-credentialed with **real-time central plan review**.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: OS** from second-step randomization, powered for HR 0.76 at 80% power (316 events). Secondary: DFS and adverse events. Final analysis triggered at 5 years of potential follow-up before the event target, leaving **270 OS events** and 72% power.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: No excess grade 4/5 AEs (**6% v 5%, P=.68**); one grade 5 per arm (hepatic failure, sepsis). Grade 3 rose to **38% v 19% (P<.001)**, driven by GI disorders (grade 3-5 any 11% v 2%), diarrhea (6% v 1%) and lymphocyte count decreased (10% v 2%). Grade 3 nonhematologic 22% v 11%, P=.004.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: **ESPAC-1** found adjuvant CXRT detrimental, but accrued 1994-2000 with split-course lower-dose 2D radiotherapy, no postoperative imaging to exclude incomplete resection or early metastasis, and no QA. **RTOG 9704** post hoc linked RT protocol deviation to worse survival, which this trial pre-empted with mandatory pretreatment review.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents resected pancreatic head adenocarcinoma progression-free after five cycles of gemcitabine-based adjuvant chemotherapy. Does not represent body/tail primaries, FOLFIRINOX-treated pts, or the neoadjuvant setting where postoperative nodal status is harder to interpret.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Accrual took almost 9 years and the analysis trigger changed, cutting power to **72%**. The N0 signal rests on **91 pts** and only **10 pts total were node-negative and margin-positive** (5 per arm), so the margin question is unanswerable here. The authors argue the observed HR 0.96 is too far from the hypothesized 0.76 for a missed true OS benefit.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Authors frame the N0 benefit as locoregional control mattering most where competing distant-failure risk is lowest, consistent with a codominant failure pattern (local failure 30%-40% after adjuvant chemotherapy). They propose neoadjuvant chemo ± CXRT and a postoperative ± CXRT trial restricted to N0 pts; SBRT substitution is explicitly unstudied.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Modern QA'd CXRT (50.4 Gy/28 fx, 81% IMRT, real-time central review) costs grade 3 toxicity 38% v 19% with no grade 4/5 excess, and buys nothing overall but 5y OS 48.1% v 28.6% in N0 pts. That is the specific population in which to raise adjuvant CXRT, and the safety benchmark that retires the ESPAC-1 objection.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: The backbone is obsolete: 67% gemcitabine alone, 28% gem+erlotinib, zero FOLFIRINOX, so the null OS result cannot be read against current adjuvant practice. For a med onc the actionable point is that adding CXRT did not raise grade 4/5 AEs (6% v 5%), so referral for the N0 discussion does not jeopardize systemic delivery.

papers.title: Adjuvant Chemotherapy ± Chemoradiotherapy for Adenocarcinoma of the Pancreatic Head: Results of the Radiotherapy Random Assignment of NRG Oncology/RTOG 0848
papers.abstract: PURPOSE To assess whether adding fluoropyrimidine sensitized radiotherapy (CXRT) to adjuvant chemotherapy improves overall survival (OS) after curative intent resection of the pancreatic head. METHODS This was a multicenter, randomized phase III, two step trial. Step 1: gemcitabine versus gemcitabine + erlotinib (previously reported). Step 2: random assignment to sixth chemotherapy cycle ± CXRT after five cycles of step 1 chemotherapy without progression. Outcomes of step 2 random assignment are reported here. Assuming 17 months median OS (chemotherapy alone), the sample size was 354 patients (hazard ratio [HR], 0.76, 80% power, one-sided α = .05, 316 OS events). OS/disease-free survival (DFS) were estimated by Kaplan-Meier and arms compared using the log-rank test. RESULTS A total of 354 patients (median age 63, 55% male, 56% performance status, 1) were randomly assigned to chemotherapy (174) or chemotherapy + CXRT (180). Univariable median and 5-year OS (90% CIs) were 2.6 years (2.1-3.1) and 23.1% (17.7-28.6) for chemotherapy alone, and 2.3 years (2.0-2.6) and 27.9% (22.2-33.6) for chemotherapy + CXRT. The OS primary end point was not met (HR, 0.96 [90% CI, 0.79 to 1.18]; one-sided P = .38, two-sided P = .77). Chemotherapy + CXRT was associated with a trend for improved DFS (univariably; HR, 0.82 [95% CI, 0.65 to 1.03]; P = .089), without increase in grade 4/5 toxicities. However, grade 3 toxicity increased (38% v 19%, P < .001). Significantly, treatment by nodal status interactions showed that CXRT improved OS ( P = .0063) and DFS ( P = .014) in node-negative patients. CONCLUSION Overall, the addition of adjuvant CXRT to adjuvant gemcitabine did not statistically significantly improve OS, DFS, or increase grade 4/5 toxicity. For node-negative patients, CXRT improved OS and DFS. These results, if confirmed in studies with current or future systemic therapies, would support the use of adjuvant/neoadjuvant CXRT for node-negative patients.
